```{python}
import sys

from shared.components import (
    chart_card,
    method_and_sources,
    prev_next,
    related_studies,
    stat_tile,
    stat_tiles,
)
from shared.glossary import glossary_popovers
from shared.outputs import read_output
from shared.paths import CASE_STUDIES, REPO_URL, ROOT

STUDY = CASE_STUDIES / "07_trade"
sys.path.insert(0, str(STUDY / "analysis"))
import figures as F  # noqa: E402

trade, prov_trade, notes_trade = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "trade_totals.csv")
sections, prov_sec, notes_sec = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "trade_sections.csv")
check, prov_check, notes_check = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "trade_crosscheck.csv")

t = trade.set_index("year")
FIRST, LAST = int(t.index.min()), int(t.index.max())
share = sections.pivot_table(index="year", columns=["flow", "sitc"], values="share_pct")
value = sections.pivot_table(index="year", columns=["flow", "sitc"], values="value_bnd_m")
E0 = int(sections[sections.flow == "exports"].year.min())  # exports by section start later


def bn(x):
    return f"B${x / 1000:.1f} bn"


def pct(x):
    return f"{x:.0f}%" if x >= 10 else f"{x:.1f}%"


low_year, high_year = int(t.balance.idxmin()), int(t.balance.idxmax())
peak_exports = int(t.exports.idxmax())
trough_after = int(t.loc[peak_exports:, "exports"].idxmin())
imports_x = t.loc[LAST, "imports"] / t.loc[FIRST, "imports"]
re_share = t.re_exports / t.exports * 100
fuel_x, chem_x = share[("exports", 3)], share[("exports", 5)]
fuel_m, mach_m = share[("imports", 3)], share[("imports", 7)]
fuel_jump = 2019  # first year mineral fuels pass 20% of imports (asserted below)
largest = value["imports"].idxmax(axis=1)  # largest import section each year
not_mach = [int(y) for y in largest.loc[: fuel_jump - 1].index if largest[y] != 7]
import_falls = int((t.imports.diff() < 0).sum())

# Stated in the text below; stop the build rather than publish them if the data changes.
assert (t.balance > 0).all(), "Not a surplus every year any more."
assert low_year == LAST - 1 and peak_exports == 2012 and trough_after == 2016
assert int(fuel_m[fuel_m > 20].index.min()) == fuel_jump and fuel_m.loc[: fuel_jump - 1].max() < 11
assert (largest.loc[fuel_jump:] == 3).all() and (largest.loc[: fuel_jump - 1] != 3).all()
assert not_mach == [2001] and largest[2001] == 6  # machinery led every year but one before
assert fuel_x.loc[E0:].min() == fuel_x.loc[LAST] and chem_x.idxmax() == LAST
assert value[("imports", 7)].loc[LAST] > value[("imports", 7)].loc[FIRST]  # share fell, value rose
assert re_share.max() < 10
assert chem_x.loc[: LAST - 2].max() < 5  # "under 5% until 2019" (chart description)
assert check.differences.sum() == 0
```

::: {.study-intro}
This case study looks at **what Brunei sold to and bought from other countries from 2000 to
2021**, using the yearly trade tables of the Department of Statistics, JPES: the value of
exports and imports, the [balance of trade]{.term term="balance-of-trade"}, and the broad
[commodity sections]{.term term="commodity-section"} the goods belong to. All values are in
Brunei dollars at [current prices]{.term term="current-prices"}. It shows **what changed, not
why**.

It asks three questions, answered in the conclusion:

1. **Did Brunei export more than it imported every year, and how did the gap change?**
2. **What does Brunei export, and how did that change from 2009 to 2021?**
3. **What does Brunei import, and how did that change from 2000 to 2021?**
:::

```{python}
stat_tiles(
    stat_tile(f"Trade surplus, {LAST}", bn(t.loc[LAST, "balance"]), "", f"(smallest: {bn(t.loc[low_year, 'balance'])} in {low_year})"),
    stat_tile(f"Imports, {LAST}", bn(t.loc[LAST, "imports"]), "", f"{imports_x:.1f}× the {FIRST} value ({bn(t.loc[FIRST, 'imports'])})"),
    stat_tile(f"Mineral fuels' share of imports, {LAST}", pct(fuel_m.loc[LAST]), "", f"({FIRST}: {pct(fuel_m.loc[FIRST])})"),
)
```

```{python}
fig, table = F.flows(trade)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Exports stayed above imports every year, but imports grew {imports_x:.0f}-fold",
    subtitle=f"Exports and imports of goods, B$ billion at current prices · {FIRST}–{LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Two lines. Exports start at {bn(t.loc[FIRST, 'exports'])} in {FIRST}, peak at "
        f"{bn(t.loc[peak_exports, 'exports'])} in {peak_exports}, fall to "
        f"{bn(t.loc[trough_after, 'exports'])} in {trough_after} and reach "
        f"{bn(t.loc[LAST, 'exports'])} in {LAST}. Imports rise from {bn(t.loc[FIRST, 'imports'])} "
        f"to {bn(t.loc[LAST, 'imports'])} and stay below exports in every year."
    ),
    provenance=prov_trade,
    table=table,
    mobile_fig=F.flows(trade, compact=True)[0],
)
```

## Exports, imports and the balance, 2000–2021

Exports were worth `{python} bn(t.loc[FIRST, "exports"])` in `{python} FIRST`. They rose to a
peak of `{python} bn(t.loc[peak_exports, "exports"])` in `{python} peak_exports`, fell to
`{python} bn(t.loc[trough_after, "exports"])` in `{python} trough_after`, and were back at
`{python} bn(t.loc[LAST, "exports"])` in `{python} LAST`. Almost all were
[domestic exports]{.term term="domestic-exports"}:
[re-exports]{.term term="re-exports"} were never more than `{python} pct(re_share.max())` of the
total.

Imports rose from `{python} bn(t.loc[FIRST, "imports"])` to
`{python} bn(t.loc[LAST, "imports"])`, falling from one year to the next only
`{python} import_falls` times. **Brunei exported more than it imported in every year**,
but the surplus changed a lot: from `{python} bn(t.loc[high_year, "balance"])` in
`{python} high_year` to `{python} bn(t.loc[low_year, "balance"])` in `{python} low_year`, the
smallest in the period, before widening again to `{python} bn(t.loc[LAST, "balance"])` in
`{python} LAST`.

```{python}
fig, table = F.balance(trade)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"The surplus was largest in {high_year} and smallest in {low_year}",
    subtitle=f"Balance of trade (exports − imports), B$ billion at current prices · {FIRST}–{LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Bar chart. The surplus is positive in every year, largest at "
        f"{bn(t.loc[high_year, 'balance'])} in {high_year} and smallest at "
        f"{bn(t.loc[low_year, 'balance'])} in {low_year}, then {bn(t.loc[LAST, 'balance'])} in {LAST}."
    ),
    provenance=prov_trade,
    table=table,
    height=300,
    mobile_fig=F.balance(trade, compact=True)[0],
)
```

## What Brunei exports, 2009–2021

The section tables for exports start in `{python} E0`. In that year, **mineral fuels (SITC
section 3, "mineral fuels, lubricants and related materials") were
`{python} pct(fuel_x.loc[E0])` of exports**. Their [share]{.term term="share-of-imports"}
stayed between `{python} pct(fuel_x.loc[: LAST - 2].min())` and
`{python} pct(fuel_x.loc[: LAST - 2].max())` until `{python} LAST - 2`, and was
`{python} pct(fuel_x.loc[LAST])` in `{python} LAST`, the lowest in the period.

Chemicals grew the most: from `{python} pct(chem_x.loc[E0])` of exports in `{python} E0` to
`{python} pct(chem_x.loc[LAST - 2])` in `{python} LAST - 2`,
`{python} pct(chem_x.loc[LAST - 1])` in `{python} LAST - 1` and
**`{python} pct(chem_x.loc[LAST])` in `{python} LAST`**
(`{python} bn(value[("exports", 5)].loc[LAST])`). The other eight sections together were never
more than `{python} pct((100 - fuel_x - chem_x).max())` of exports.

```{python}
fig, table = F.export_mix(sections)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Mineral fuels fell to {pct(fuel_x.loc[LAST])} of exports as chemicals rose to {pct(chem_x.loc[LAST])}",
    subtitle=f"Share of exports by commodity section, % · {E0}–{LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Three lines. Mineral fuels stay between {pct(fuel_x.min())} and {pct(fuel_x.max())} of "
        f"exports, ending at {pct(fuel_x.loc[LAST])} in {LAST}. Chemicals stay under 5% until "
        f"{LAST - 2}, then rise to {pct(chem_x.loc[LAST])}. All other sections stay low."
    ),
    provenance=prov_sec,
    table=table,
    mobile_fig=F.export_mix(sections, compact=True)[0],
)
```

## What Brunei imports, 2000–2021

Until `{python} fuel_jump - 1`, **machinery and transport equipment was the largest import
section in every year but one** (`{python} not_mach[0]`, when it was manufactured goods). It
was `{python} pct(mach_m.loc[FIRST])` of imports in `{python} FIRST`. Mineral fuels were
`{python} pct(fuel_m.loc[FIRST])` in `{python} FIRST` and no more than
`{python} pct(fuel_m.loc[: fuel_jump - 1].max())` in any year to `{python} fuel_jump - 1`.

That changed in `{python} fuel_jump`: **mineral fuel imports rose from
`{python} bn(value[("imports", 3)].loc[fuel_jump - 1])` to
`{python} bn(value[("imports", 3)].loc[fuel_jump])`**, or `{python} pct(fuel_m.loc[fuel_jump])`
of imports, and they were the largest section in every year after. By `{python} LAST` they
were `{python} bn(value[("imports", 3)].loc[LAST])`, `{python} pct(fuel_m.loc[LAST])` of all
imports. Machinery and transport fell to `{python} pct(mach_m.loc[LAST])` of imports, although
its value still grew, from `{python} bn(value[("imports", 7)].loc[FIRST])` to
`{python} bn(value[("imports", 7)].loc[LAST])`.

```{python}
fig, table = F.import_mix(sections)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"From {fuel_jump}, mineral fuels became Brunei's largest import",
    subtitle=f"Share of imports by commodity section, % · {FIRST}–{LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Four lines. Mineral fuels stay under {pct(fuel_m.loc[: fuel_jump - 1].max())} of imports "
        f"until {fuel_jump - 1}, jump to {pct(fuel_m.loc[fuel_jump])} in {fuel_jump} and reach "
        f"{pct(fuel_m.loc[LAST])} in {LAST}. Machinery and transport falls from "
        f"{pct(mach_m.loc[FIRST])} to {pct(mach_m.loc[LAST])}. Manufactured goods and all other "
        f"sections stay lower."
    ),
    provenance=prov_sec,
    table=table,
    mobile_fig=F.import_mix(sections, compact=True)[0],
)
```

## Conclusion

- **Did Brunei export more than it imported every year, and how did the gap change?** Yes:
  there was a surplus in every year from `{python} FIRST` to `{python} LAST`. It was largest
  in `{python} high_year` (`{python} bn(t.loc[high_year, "balance"])`) and smallest in
  `{python} low_year` (`{python} bn(t.loc[low_year, "balance"])`), as imports grew
  `{python} f"{imports_x:.1f}"`-fold over the period.
- **What does Brunei export, and how did that change from 2009 to 2021?** Mostly mineral
  fuels, but less so by the end: from `{python} pct(fuel_x.loc[E0])` of exports in
  `{python} E0` to `{python} pct(fuel_x.loc[LAST])` in `{python} LAST`, while chemicals rose
  from `{python} pct(chem_x.loc[E0])` to `{python} pct(chem_x.loc[LAST])`.
- **What does Brunei import, and how did that change from 2000 to 2021?** Machinery and
  transport equipment was the largest section until `{python} fuel_jump - 1` (in every year
  but one). From `{python} fuel_jump`, mineral fuels were the largest import section, reaching
  `{python} pct(fuel_m.loc[LAST])` of imports in `{python} LAST`.

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" title="What this doesn't tell us"}
- **Why trade changed.** The data shows when and by how much values changed, not what caused
  the changes.
- **Prices or quantities.** These are values at current prices. A rise or fall can come from
  prices, from the amounts traded, or both, and the tables don't separate them.
- **Which products.** Each section mixes many goods, and the published tables don't break
  them down, so they can't show which mineral fuels or chemicals were traded.
- **Trading partners and services.** Countries are in separate tables not used here, and
  services (such as tourism or transport) are not part of these figures.
- **After `{python} LAST`.** The latest year published is `{python} LAST`. The edition used
  says 2000–2020 on its dataset page, but its table includes `{python} LAST`.
:::
